question: For Azure Blob backup, how long should I keep blob versions in the storage account relative to my backup retention, and will the Backup vault clean up old versions for me?
gold_facts: For operational backup, set version retention to backup retention plus 7 days (e.g. 30 days -> 37 days).
For vaulted backup only, version retention can be reduced after the first successful backup, keeping versions at least 7 days after backup completion.
If both operational and vaulted backup are used, apply the higher of the two retention requirements.
The Backup vault does not delete or reconcile blob versions in the source storage account; use Lifecycle Management policies or manual cleanup.

B.text: For operational backup, set blob version retention to backup retention plus seven days (e.g., if backup retention is 30 days, set version retention to 37 days) [1]. Azure Backup does not manage blob versioning or delete/reconcile blob versions in the source storage account; version cleanup must be managed separately using Lifecycle Management (LCM) policies or manual configuration [2]. Azure Blob backup also requires a lifecycle management policy with a minimum retention of seven days for blob versions to avoid backup failures [3].

sources.paraphrase: For operational backup, set blob version retention to backup retention plus seven days (e.g., if backup retention is 30 days, set version retention to 37 days).

documents.title: FAQ-Azure Blob Backup
documents.text:
[FAQ-Azure Blob Backup › FAQ-Azure Blob Backup]
Frequently asked questions about Azure Blob Backup
==================================================

This article answers frequently asked questions about Azure Blob Backup. For more information on the Azure Blob backup region availability, supported scenarios, and limitations, see the [support matrix](blob-backup-support-matrix).


Why does Azure Backup require to keep all versions for Blob backups?
--------------------------------------------------------------------

Azure Backup doesn’t manage blob versioning because it’s a storage account feature. When you enable vaulted backup, Azure Backup uses the Object Replication Service (ORS) to replicate blobs, including all versions, to the Backup Vault.
 The Backup Vault applies retention policies, such as 42 days, at the backup layer and not at the source storage account. Azure Backup doesn't change versioning settings in the storage account, as there might be independent compliance or operational requirements for retaining versions.


Does Backup vault reconcile or delete older blob versions in the source account?
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

No, the Backup vault doesn't delete or reconcile blob versions in the source storage account. The retention policy applies only to restore points stored in the vault. For blob version cleanup in the source account, manage it separately using Lifecycle Management (LCM) policies or manual configuration.


Can I align blob versioning retention with my backup policy, such as 42 days?
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

Yes, you can configure blob version retention in the storage account, but it works independently of the backup policy.


* For operational backup, set version retention to backup retention plus seven days. For example, if backup retention is 30 days, set version retention to 37 days.
* For vaulted backup only, reduce version retention after the first successful backup. We recommend you to keep versions for at least seven days after backup completion, or longer for large accounts with frequent changes.
* If you use both operational and vaulted backup, apply the higher of the two retention requirements.


What is the impact on existing recovery points when I modify the Backup policy?
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

With the modification of backup instance, you can assign new policy. Policy are applied only on future recovery points. Past recovery points are still retained as per the previous policy's retention period.


What happens when account has blobs in archive tier?
----------------------------------------------------

Archive blobs present before backup is configured are skipped during backup. This behavior is expected and does not cause failures, delays, or errors in the backup job. If blobs are moved to archive after backup configuration, the backup copy in the vault will not inherit the Archive tier, and backup continues without issues.

sources.paraphrase: Azure Backup does not manage blob versioning or delete/reconcile blob versions in the source storage account; version cleanup must be managed separately using Lifecycle Management (LCM) policies or manual configuration.
Azure Blob backup requires a lifecycle management policy with a minimum retention of seven days for blob versions to avoid backup failures.

documents.title: Azure Blob backup
documents.text:
[Azure Blob backup › Azure Blob backup]


UserErrorBlobContainerDeletedDuringBackup
-----------------------------------------

**Error code**: `UserErrorBlobContainerDeletedDuringBackup`

**Error message**: The backup failed due to one or more blob containers deleted in the backup job duration.

**Recommended action**: We recommend to avoid tampering with blob containers while a backup job is in progress.

UserErrorBlobVersionArchivedAndContainerDeletedDuringBackup
-----------------------------------------------------------

**Error code**: `UserErrorBlobVersionArchivedAndContainerDeletedDuringBackup`

**Error message**: The backup failed due to one or more blob versions are moving to the archive tier and one or more containers deleted in the backup job duration.

**Recommended action**: We recommend to avoid tampering with blob versions and blob containers while a backup job is in progress.

UserErrorBlobVersionDeletedAndContainerDeletedDuringBackup
----------------------------------------------------------

**Error code**: `UserErrorBlobVersionDeletedAndContainerDeletedDuringBackup`

**Error message** \- The backup failed due to one or more blob versions getting deleted or container getting deleted in the backup job duration.

**Recommended action**: We recommend to avoid tampering with blob versions and containers while a backup job is in progress. Ensure the minimum retention configured for versions in lifecycle management policy is seven days.


UserErrorBlobVersionArchivedDeletedAndContainerDeletedDuringBackup
------------------------------------------------------------------

**Error code**: `UserErrorBlobVersionArchivedDeletedAndContainerDeletedDuringBackup`

**Error message**: The backup failed due to one or more blob versions moving to the archive tier, blob version getting deleted, and container getting deleted in the backup job duration.

**Recommended action**: We recommend to avoid tampering with blob versions and containers while a backup job is in progress. Ensure the minimum retention configured for versions in lifecycle management policy is seven days.


LongRunningOperationTrackingFailure
-----------------------------------

**Error code**: `LongRunningOperationTrackingFailure`

**Error message**: Failed to track the long\-running operation. The operation is still running and is expected to complete.

This error is usually seen for operational tier restore failure due to PITR still running in background. And potentially should complete.

**Recommended action**: Track further progress on the operation in storage account activity log.

A.text:
For operational backup, set blob version retention to backup retention plus seven days (e.g., 37 days for a 30-day backup retention) [1]. For vaulted backup only, reduce version retention after the first successful backup, keeping versions for at least seven days after backup completion—or longer for large accounts with frequent changes [1]. If you use both operational and vaulted backup, apply the higher of the two retention requirements [1].

The Backup vault will not clean up old versions for you: it doesn't delete or reconcile blob versions in the source storage account, and its retention policy applies only to restore points stored in the vault. You must manage version cleanup in the source account separately using Lifecycle Management (LCM) policies or manual configuration [1]. Azure Backup also doesn't change versioning settings in the storage account, since there may be independent compliance or operational requirements for retaining versions [1].

question: When I query Azure Backup data in Log Analytics with the built-in system functions, do I get today's records, can I modify those functions, and do they include the legacy AzureDiagnostics table?
gold_facts: System functions return data only up to the last completed day (UTC); the current partial day requires querying the raw LA tables.
System functions are maintained by Microsoft and cannot be edited; use saved functions in Log Analytics for editable ones.
The ExcludeLegacyEvent parameter controls whether the legacy AzureDiagnostics table is queried; its default is true (resource-specific tables only).

A.text:
When using Azure Backup's built-in system functions in Log Analytics:

- **Modifiability:** The system functions are maintained by Microsoft and their definitions cannot be edited by users; if you need editable functions, you can create saved functions in Log Analytics [3].

- **Legacy AzureDiagnostics table:** The system functions let you choose whether to query data from both the legacy diagnostics event (AzureBackupReport in AzureDiagnostics mode) and resource-specific tables, with deduplication [4], or only from resource-specific events [6]. This is controlled via the ExcludeLegacyEvent parameter [5]: when ExcludeLegacyEvent is true (the default), queries exclude the legacy AzureDiagnostics table and use only resource-specific tables; when false, queries include both the AzureDiagnostics table and resource-specific tables [2][7].

- **Today's records:** I don't have enough information to answer that from the available sources.

sources.paraphrase: Azure Backup can query data from the legacy AzureDiagnostics table unless ExcludeLegacyEvent is true; ExcludeLegacyEvent defaults to true which limits queries to only resource-specific tables.

documents.title: System Functions
documents.text:
[System Functions › System Functions]

* **Reduces possibility of custom queries breaking**: If Azure Backup introduces improvements to the schema of the underlying LA tables to accommodate future reporting scenarios, the definition of the functions will also be updated to take into account the schema changes. Thus, if you use system functions for creating custom queries, your queries won't break, even if there are changes in the underlying schema of the tables.

Note

System functions are maintained by Microsoft and their definitions cannot be edited by users. If you require editable functions, you can create [saved functions](/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/logs/functions) in LA.

Types of system functions offered by Azure Backup
-------------------------------------------------

* **Core functions**: These are functions that help you query any of the key Azure Backup entities, such as Backup Instances, Vaults, Policies, Jobs and Billing Entities. For example, the **\_AzureBackup\_getBackupInstances** function returns a list of all the backup instances that exist in your environment as of the latest completed day (in UTC). The parameters and returned schema for each of these core functions are summarized below in this article.
* **Trend functions**: These are functions that return historical records for your backup\-related entities (for example, backup instances, billing groups) and allow you to get daily, weekly and monthly trend information on key metrics (for example, Count, Storage consumed) pertaining to these entities. The parameters and returned schema for each of these trend functions are summarized below in this article.

Note

Currently, system functions return data for up to the last completed day (in UTC). Data for the current partial day isn't returned. So if you are looking to retrieve records for the current day, you'll need to use the raw LA tables.

List of system functions
------------------------

### Core Functions

documents.title: System Functions
documents.text:
[System Functions › System Functions]
System Functions for Azure Backup
=================================

This article describes how to write custom queries on Azure Monitor Logs using system functions.

Azure Backup provides a set of functions, called system functions or solution functions that are available by default in your Log Analytics (LA) workspaces.

These functions operate on data in the [raw Azure Backup tables](backup-azure-reports-data-model) in LA and return formatted data that helps you easily retrieve information of all your backup\-related entities, using simple queries. Users can pass parameters to these functions to filter the data that is returned by these functions.

We recommend you to use system functions for querying your backup data in LA workspaces for creating custom reports, as they provide a number of benefits, as detailed in the section below.

Benefits of using system functions
----------------------------------

* **Simpler queries**: Using functions helps you reduce the number of joins needed in your queries. By default, the functions return ‘flattened’ schemas that incorporate all information pertaining to the entity (backup instance, job, vault, and so on) being queried. For example, if you need to get a list of successful backup jobs by backup item name and its associated container, a simple call to the **\_AzureBackup\_getJobs()** function will give you all of this information for each job. On the other hand, querying the raw tables directly would require you to perform multiple joins between [AddonAzureBackupJobs](backup-azure-reports-data-model#addonazurebackupjobs) and [CoreAzureBackup](backup-azure-reports-data-model#coreazurebackup) tables.
* **Smoother transition from the legacy diagnostics event**: Using system functions helps you transition smoothly from the [legacy diagnostics event](backup-azure-diagnostic-events#legacy-event) (AzureBackupReport in AzureDiagnostics mode) to the [resource\-specific events](backup-azure-diagnostic-events#diagnostics-events-available-for-azure-backup-users). All the system functions provided by Azure Backup allows you to specify a parameter that lets you choose whether the function should query data only from the resource\-specific tables, or query data from both the legacy table and the resource\-specific tables (with deduplication of records).

	+ If you have successfully migrated to the resource\-specific tables, you can choose to exclude the legacy table from being queried by the function.
	+ If you're currently in the process of migration and have some data in the legacy tables which you require for analysis, you can choose to include the legacy table. When the transition is complete, and you no longer need data from the legacy table, you can update the value of the parameter passed to the function in your queries, to exclude the legacy table.
	+ If you're still using only the legacy table, the functions will still work if you choose to include the legacy table via the same parameter. However, it's recommended to [switch to the resource\-specific tables](backup-azure-diagnostic-events#steps-to-move-to-new-diagnostics-settings-for-a-log-analytics-workspace) at the earliest.

By default, the functions return ‘flattened’ schemas that incorporate all information pertaining to the entity (backup instance, job, vault, and so on) being queried. For example, if you need to get a list of successful backup jobs by backup item name and its associated container, a simple call to the **\_AzureBackup\_getJobs()** function will give you all of this information for each job. On the other hand, querying the raw tables directly would require you to perform multiple joins between [AddonAzureBackupJobs](backup-azure-reports-data-model#addonazurebackupjobs) and [CoreAzureBackup](backup-azure-reports-data-model#coreazurebackup) tables.
* **Smoother transition from the legacy diagnostics event**: Using system functions helps you transition smoothly from the [legacy diagnostics event](backup-azure-diagnostic-events#legacy-event) (AzureBackupReport in AzureDiagnostics mode) to the [resource\-specific events](backup-azure-diagnostic-events#diagnostics-events-available-for-azure-backup-users). All the system functions provided by Azure Backup allows you to specify a parameter that lets you choose whether the function should query data only from the resource\-specific tables, or query data from both the legacy table and the resource\-specific tables (with deduplication of records).

	+ If you have successfully migrated to the resource\-specific tables, you can choose to exclude the legacy table from being queried by the function.
	+ If you're currently in the process of migration and have some data in the legacy tables which you require for analysis, you can choose to include the legacy table. When the transition is complete, and you no longer need data from the legacy table, you can update the value of the parameter passed to the function in your queries, to exclude the legacy table.
	+ If you're still using only the legacy table, the functions will still work if you choose to include the legacy table via the same parameter. However, it's recommended to [switch to the resource\-specific tables](backup-azure-diagnostic-events#steps-to-move-to-new-diagnostics-settings-for-a-log-analytics-workspace) at the earliest.
* **Reduces possibility of custom queries breaking**: If Azure Backup introduces improvements to the schema of the underlying LA tables to accommodate future reporting scenarios, the definition of the functions will also be updated to take into account the schema changes. Thus, if you use system functions for creating custom queries, your queries won't break, even if there are changes in the underlying schema of the tables.

Note

System functions are maintained by Microsoft and their definitions cannot be edited by users. If you require editable functions, you can create [saved functions](/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/logs/functions) in LA.

documents.title: System Functions
documents.text:
System Functions
System Functions for Azure Backup > Types of system functions offered by Azure Backup

* **Core functions**: These are functions that help you query any of the key Azure Backup entities, such as Backup Instances, Vaults, Policies, Jobs and Billing Entities. For example, the **\_AzureBackup\_getBackupInstances** function returns a list of all the backup instances that exist in your environment as of the latest completed day (in UTC). The parameters and returned schema for each of these core functions are summarized below in this article.
* **Trend functions**: These are functions that return historical records for your backup\-related entities (for example, backup instances, billing groups) and allow you to get daily, weekly and monthly trend information on key metrics (for example, Count, Storage consumed) pertaining to these entities. The parameters and returned schema for each of these trend functions are summarized below in this article.

Note

Currently, system functions return data for up to the last completed day (in UTC). Data for the current partial day isn't returned. So if you are looking to retrieve records for the current day, you'll need to use the raw LA tables.

question: Are snapshots vaulted to Cohesity FortKnox immutable by default, and what mechanism enforces it?
gold_facts: Snapshots vaulted in a FortKnox cloud vault are DataLocked by default.
DataLock makes storage WORM-compliant so backups and archives cannot be tampered with or deleted.
FortKnox uses AWS S3 Object Lock as the DataLock mechanism.

A.text: Yes. Snapshots vaulted in the Cohesity FortKnox cloud vault are DataLocked by default [2], and DataLock is enabled by default for backups to Cloud Vault, preventing data deletion until expiry [3]. The enforcement mechanism is AWS S3 Object Lock, which FortKnox uses to DataLock the snapshots [1].

sources.paraphrase: Cohesity FortKnox uses AWS S3 Object Lock as the mechanism to DataLock the snapshots.

documents.title: DataLock
documents.text:
[DataLock › DataLock]
## DataLock

DataLock enables your storage to be WORM-compliant. When it is enabled, your data such as backups and archives cannot be tampered or deleted. This results in prevention from ransomware attacks on your data.
 By default, the snapshots vaulted in a cloud vault are DataLocked. Cohesity FortKnox uses AWS S3 Object Lock as the mechanism to DataLock the snapshots.

sources.paraphrase: Snapshots vaulted in the Cohesity FortKnox cloud vault are DataLocked by default.

documents.title: Get Started
documents.text:
[Get Started › Get Started]
Before you start on Cohesity FortKnox, it is important that you plan and decide on aspects such as:


- l Data from which cluster(s) should be vaulted in the cloud?
- l Which workloads such as Virtual Machines and Databases should be vaulted to the cloud?
- l In which Amazon Web Services region should the cloud vault be created?
- l How long do you want to retain the snapshots in a cloud vault?

- l Do you want to use Cohesity-managed key management service (KMS) or Selfmanaged KMS?

Note: Self-managed KMS option supports only Amazon Web Services KMS.

- l What would be the backup window ?


## Cohesity Clusters

Cohesity FortKnox vaults data from your cluster to the cloud. To achieve this, it's important for you to plan and decide on the clusters whose data will be sent to a cloud vault.
 After you decide on the clusters, you have to ensure that these clusters are associated with the Cohesity Helios account that includes Cohesity FortKnox. For more information on the supported cluster types, see Clusters.


## Workloads

Cohesity FortKnox allows you to recover workloads such as virtual machines and databases. For more information, see Supported Workloads, Clusters, and Regions.

For more information on workflows that are supported for each workload, see Supported Workflows.


## Snapshot Retention

The snapshots that are vaulted in the cloud vault are DataLocked by default and can be deleted after the retention period. Before you start using Cohesity FortKnox, It's important that you decide on how long you want to retain the snapshots in a cloud vault.

[Prerequisites › Prerequisites]
1. Transfer to : Choose a cloud vault where you want to transfer or backup your data.
2. Every : Choose either Run or any time interval to determine how often data should be backed up to a Cloud Vault. This defines the protection schedule for capturing backups.
3. Retain for : Specify for how many days the backups are retained in a Cloud Vault.
4. l For AWS, the minimum retention allowed is 30 days for warm vault and 90 days for cold vault.

- l For Azure, the minimum retention allowed is 30 days for warm vault and 120 days for cold vault.

You can configure different retention time for different policies. For Free Trial users, the retention period is set to 30 days.

Note: By default, DataLock is enabled for backups to Cloud Vault. This means the data cannot be deleted once it is sent to the vault till it expires. After the expiry date, the data will be automatically removed.

4. You can optionally choose to Transfer only successful runs .
5. Select Add .
6. On the Cloud Vault Protection page, select Continue .

The Cloud Vault Quorum Group page appears.

You've added Cloud Vault Protection to the policy in your cluster. The vaulting task to the cloud vault is initiated in the next protection run.

Note: You can view the vault added to the policy from the Cohesity Data Cloud (Self-managed), however, you cannot modify it. Vaulting can be configured only from the Policies tab in the Protection page in Cohesity FortKnox.

## Create Cloud Vault Quorum Group

In Cohesity FortKnox, you can define a group of users called a quorum group who can collectively decide whether the operations initiated by a FortKnox user are allowed to be executed or not.

Follow the steps below to create a quorum group.

1. Select Create Quorum Group .
2. Under Group Details , enter the Name of the quorum group, choose an Operation Target , and add a Description (Optional).
3. Under Operations , Recover from FortKnox Vault and Recover Metadata from FortKnox Vault are selected by default.

Note: An operation can be assigned to only one quorum group. This means an operation, for example, Recover from FortKnox Vault , can be approved by only one Quorum group.

4. Under Approvers , add the members of the quorum group. The list of members are populated based on the users available in your Cohesity Data Cloud account.
5. Set the Approval Quorum . You can either select All Members or set a minimum value of members required to approve any requests.
6. Set Approval Workflow . You can enter a time value after which the defined action, either Accept or Deny , will be taken automatically.
7. Select Create . You've created the quorum group.
8. Select Complete .

The Dashboard page appears.

You've now successfully completed the onboarding steps to access Cohesity FortKnox .

documents.text:
Edit Policies
Edit Policies

In Cohesity FortKnox, you can edit the policies that are available in the Cohesity clusters associated with the Cohesity Data Cloud user account and add Cloud Vault configurations to policies.

A policy is a reusable set of settings that define how and when objects are protected, replicated and vaulted. You select which standard policy to use when configuring a Protection Group. A Protection Group uses the schedules and settings defined in the policy to determine when and how backups are captured, vaulted or replicated.

You can use the default standard policies or create your own custom policies.

Tip: Policies eliminate the effort to repetitively define the same settings for different sources and protection groups and therefore, saves time for you.

Note: When a policy includes a Cloud Vault, Smart Retention Adjustment protects your local backups from being deleted before your data is safely copied to its secondary target. If a Cloud Vault (or Replication or Archive) task is cancelled or fails after a successful local backup, Smart Retention Adjustment extends the retention of the local copy to match the failed target's retention. Smart Retention Adjustment is enabled by default. For more information, see Smart Retention Adjustment.

Follow the steps below to add Cloud Vault protection to a policy.

1. In FortKnox , navigate to Cloud Vaults > Protection .
2. The Activity tab on the Protection page appears.

3. Under the Policy column, select the policy name and select Edit .

question: How many Cohesity FortKnox cloud vaults can I create in one region, and what do I need in order to use cold storage vaults?
gold_facts: Up to 10 cloud vaults can be created in a region, with a name chosen at creation.
A cloud vault's storage class can be Warm or Cold.
Cold storage cloud vaults require the FortKnox Cold Vault entitlement.

B.text:
You can create multiple cloud vaults in a region — up to 10 — and choose a desired name for the vaults during creation [1]. A Region in FortKnox is used to provision one or multiple vaults [3].

To use cold storage vaults, you need the FortKnox Cold Vault entitlement [2]. FortKnox supports storing data to cold storage cloud vaults in addition to existing warm vaults, with a storage class choice of Warm or Cold during creation [4]. Note that only Warm cloud vaults are supported in Microsoft Azure (Cold vaults are not supported) [5]. Cold vaults are available for AWS and GCP, with a minimum retention of 90 days for AWS and 365 days for GCP [10].

sources.paraphrase: Cohesity FortKnox supports creating multiple cloud vaults (up to 10) in a region and allows choosing a desired name for the vaults during creation.

[March 2023 › March 2023]
## March 2023

## Support for Multiple Cloud Vaults in a Region

You can now create multiple cloud vaults (up to 10) in a region and choose your desired name for the vaults during its creation.


## Support for Cold Storage Cloud Vaults

In addition to the existing warm vaults, you can now store your data to cold storage cloud vaults. While creating a cloud vault, you can choose a storage class, Warm or Cold .

Note: The Cold storage cloud vault is available only if you've purchased FortKnox Cold Vault entitlement. For more information, see Create Cloud Vault.


## Support for New Workloads

Cohesity FortKnox now supports the following workloads.

Note: Instant Volume Mount and Clone operation is not supported for the following workloads. Additionally, Cohesity Agent-based backups, AWS Native snapshots, and Azure Native snapshots are not supported.


- l File-based and VDI-based SQL backups
- l Nutanix Acropolis Hypervisor (AHV)
- l AIX Server

- l Amazon EC2
- l Azure VMs

## Cloud Vault

documents.title: Prerequisites
documents.text:
[Prerequisites › Prerequisites]
## Create Cloud Vault

A cloud vault is a destination where you can backup your Cohesity cluster data and recover it to the original or a new location. Once it is created, the data from the cluster is vaulted to the cloud vault.

Follow the steps below to create a cloud vault.

1. On the Welcome to FortKnox page, select Create Cloud Vault
2. .

You can select Cancel to complete the steps later and continue to use Cohesity Data Cloud.

2. On the Create Cloud Vault dialog box, choose a Region .

A Region is used to provision one or multiple vaults.

3. Choose a Storage Class .

Storage class for the vaults can be Warm or Cold for AWS, Warm or Warm LRS (Locally Redundant Storage) or Cold LRS for Azure, and Warm or Cold for GCP. The options available to you are based on your FortKnox entitlements.

1. Warm : A warm vault created on an AWS Region leverages Amazon S3 Standard Infrequent Access (S3-IA), and requires a minimum retention of 30 days. Starting with Cohesity release 7.1.2\_u4, all new vault data is stored in the Amazon S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval storage tier.

Similarly, a warm vault created on a Microsoft Azure Region leverages Azure Cool Blob Storage.

A warm vault created on a GCP region leverages GCP Coldline storage and requires a minimum retention of 30 days.

When using any warm vault, the recovery starts immediately upon initiation.

2. Cold : A cold vault created on an AWS Region leverages Amazon S3-Glacier Flexible Retrieval (FR), and requires a minimum retention of 90 days.
2. Similarly, a cold vault created on a GCP Region leverages GCP Archive storage and requires a minimum retention of 365 days.
3. Warm LRS : A warm LRS vault created on a Microsoft Azure Region leverages Azure Cold Blob LRS storage. It requires a minimum retention of 90 days.

Note: Azure Warm LRS is supported only on cluster versions 7.3 and later.

4. Cold LRS : A cold LRS vault created on a Microsoft Azure Region leverages Azure Archive Blob LRS storage. It requires a minimum retention of 180 days.

Note: Azure LRS maintains three copies of data within a single data center in the selected primary region.

4. Choose a key management service from Select Encryption Option . For more information, see Key Management.

Note: Azure and GCP vaults support only Cohesity KMS.

## 5. Click Create .

The provisioning of the cloud vault has started. The selected region is displayed in the list and the status is shown as Provisioning . When the status changes to Provisioned , the map shows a green bubble that signifies the location of the Cloud Vault.

Note: If FortKnox vault provisioning fails, exit the onboarding wizard, go to Vault Configuration, and retry. Vault will provision successfully after some time.

On the Cloud Vault Protection page, you have to add the cloud vault protection to the policies that are available in the cluster. Follow the steps below to add the cloud vault protection to a policy.

1. Select Add Cloud Vault Protection .
2. Choose a Cluster and a Policy
3. .

The policy details are displayed.

3. Select Continue .

The Add Cloud Vault Protection to Policy appears.

documents.title: Prerequisites
documents.text:
[Prerequisites › Prerequisites]
1. Transfer to : Choose a cloud vault where you want to transfer or backup your data.
2. Every : Choose either Run or any time interval to determine how often data should be backed up to a Cloud Vault. This defines the protection schedule for capturing backups.
3. Retain for : Specify for how many days the backups are retained in a Cloud Vault.
4. l For AWS, the minimum retention allowed is 30 days for warm vault and 90 days for cold vault.

- l For Azure, the minimum retention allowed is 30 days for warm vault and 120 days for cold vault.

You can configure different retention time for different policies. For Free Trial users, the retention period is set to 30 days.

Note: By default, DataLock is enabled for backups to Cloud Vault. This means the data cannot be deleted once it is sent to the vault till it expires. After the expiry date, the data will be automatically removed.

4. You can optionally choose to Transfer only successful runs .
5. Select Add .
6. On the Cloud Vault Protection page, select Continue .

The Cloud Vault Quorum Group page appears.

You've added Cloud Vault Protection to the policy in your cluster. The vaulting task to the cloud vault is initiated in the next protection run.

Note: You can view the vault added to the policy from the Cohesity Data Cloud (Self-managed), however, you cannot modify it. Vaulting can be configured only from the Policies tab in the Protection page in Cohesity FortKnox.

## Create Cloud Vault Quorum Group

In Cohesity FortKnox, you can define a group of users called a quorum group who can collectively decide whether the operations initiated by a FortKnox user are allowed to be executed or not.

Follow the steps below to create a quorum group.

1. Select Create Quorum Group .
2. Under Group Details , enter the Name of the quorum group, choose an Operation Target , and add a Description (Optional).
3. Under Operations , Recover from FortKnox Vault and Recover Metadata from FortKnox Vault are selected by default.

Note: An operation can be assigned to only one quorum group. This means an operation, for example, Recover from FortKnox Vault , can be approved by only one Quorum group.

4. Under Approvers , add the members of the quorum group. The list of members are populated based on the users available in your Cohesity Data Cloud account.
5. Set the Approval Quorum . You can either select All Members or set a minimum value of members required to approve any requests.
6. Set Approval Workflow . You can enter a time value after which the defined action, either Accept or Deny , will be taken automatically.
7. Select Create . You've created the quorum group.
8. Select Complete .

The Dashboard page appears.

You've now successfully completed the onboarding steps to access Cohesity FortKnox .

[Cohesity Data Cloud › Cohesity Data Cloud]

- l Scale and simplicity -Manage your entire data estate easily across data centers, edge sites, and public cloud environments.

- l 3rd Party Extensibility -Connect Cohesity Data Cloud to your other IT investments to improve visibility and streamline operations.


Cohesity Data Cloud includes the following products:


- l DataProtect-Offers a unified view and global management of all your Cohesity clusters, whether on-premises, in the cloud, or as Virtual Editions, regardless of the cluster size. You can easily connect your clusters to Helios and access them from anywhere using an internet connection and your Cohesity Support Portal credentials. It simplifies cluster management and enables efficient monitoring and control across your entire infrastructure.

- l Cloud Protection Service-With Cloud Protection Service, you can embrace a more predictable OpEx cost model, streamline backup operations across the hybrid cloud, and harness the power of your data for greater possibilities. By signing up, connecting, and initiating data protection, you can get started within minutes, ensuring your valuable data is safe and secure. Experience the convenience and efficiency of our seamless cloud-based solution for all your backup needs.

- l NetBackup-Offers a unified view and global management of all your NetBackup domains from a single interface. It provides a unified view and control of the entire data estate across the edge, data center, and cloud. It allows you to easily monitor and manage your data protection, application resiliency, and compliance activities from one location.

- l Security Center-Provides a comprehensive suite of security features, including Threat Protection, Data Classification, Cyber Vaulting, and Platform Security, all conveniently accessible from a single unified platform.
- l FortKnox-An award-winning cyber-vaulting solution that offers a SaaS-based data isolation and recovery platform that securely stores an immutable copy of data in a Cohesity-managed cloud vault.


- l RecoveryAgent-Simplifies the bulk recovery of backup object(s) for supported workloads on Cohesity clusters managed on Cohesity Helios. It enables you to run threat scans and rehearsal operations on recovery groups, helping to identify and mitigate potential threats before restoring data to your environment.

- l Gaia-Harness the potential of your most important enterprise data and gain deep meaningful insights and learnings into your organization and data with Cohesity's AIpowered conversational search solution.
- l Platform Insights-Optimize, plan, and scale your data management by providing insights into your cluster's storage and load utilization, along with other essential performance metrics.

- l SmartFiles-Do more with your data with software-defined file and object services for the hybrid cloud.
- l SiteContinuity-Simplifies business continuity and disaster recovery with automated failover and failback orchestration for your mission-critical workloads.

- l IT Analytics-Provides unified visibility across multi-vendor storage, backup, and virtual infrastructures to on-premises and multi-cloud environments. It provides consolidated reporting, predictive analytics, and automated alerts to improve data reliability and reduce operational costs.

documents.text:
[Prerequisites › Prerequisites]
## Create Cloud Vault

A cloud vault is a destination where you can backup your Cohesity cluster data and recover it to the original or a new location. Once it is created, the data from the cluster is vaulted to the cloud vault.

Follow the steps below to create a cloud vault.

1. On the Welcome to FortKnox page, select Create Cloud Vault
2. .

You can select Cancel to complete the steps later and continue to use Cohesity Data Cloud.

2. On the Create Cloud Vault dialog box, choose a Region .

A Region is used to provision one or multiple vaults.

3. Choose a Storage Class .

Storage class for the vaults can be Warm or Cold for AWS, Warm or Warm LRS (Locally Redundant Storage) or Cold LRS for Azure, and Warm or Cold for GCP. The options available to you are based on your FortKnox entitlements.

1. Warm : A warm vault created on an AWS Region leverages Amazon S3 Standard Infrequent Access (S3-IA), and requires a minimum retention of 30 days. Starting with Cohesity release 7.1.2\_u4, all new vault data is stored in the Amazon S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval storage tier.

Similarly, a warm vault created on a Microsoft Azure Region leverages Azure Cool Blob Storage.

A warm vault created on a GCP region leverages GCP Coldline storage and requires a minimum retention of 30 days.

When using any warm vault, the recovery starts immediately upon initiation.

2. Cold : A cold vault created on an AWS Region leverages Amazon S3-Glacier Flexible Retrieval (FR), and requires a minimum retention of 90 days.
2. Similarly, a cold vault created on a GCP Region leverages GCP Archive storage and requires a minimum retention of 365 days.
3. Warm LRS : A warm LRS vault created on a Microsoft Azure Region leverages Azure Cold Blob LRS storage. It requires a minimum retention of 90 days.

Note: Azure Warm LRS is supported only on cluster versions 7.3 and later.

4. Cold LRS : A cold LRS vault created on a Microsoft Azure Region leverages Azure Archive Blob LRS storage. It requires a minimum retention of 180 days.

Note: Azure LRS maintains three copies of data within a single data center in the selected primary region.

4. Choose a key management service from Select Encryption Option . For more information, see Key Management.

Note: Azure and GCP vaults support only Cohesity KMS.

## 5. Click Create .

The provisioning of the cloud vault has started. The selected region is displayed in the list and the status is shown as Provisioning . When the status changes to Provisioned , the map shows a green bubble that signifies the location of the Cloud Vault.

[Prerequisites › Prerequisites]
## Cohesity Cluster

Cohesity FortKnox vaults your cluster data. Only the data which is locally backed up by Cohesity can be vaulted to FortKnox. Therefore, you would need to have data protection capabilities and SmartFiles deployed in a Cohesity cluster.

## Connect Clusters to Cohesity Helios

Cohesity FortKnox vaults the data residing in a Cohesity cluster to a cloud vault. To make this happen, FortKnox uses the clusters that are connected to Cohesity Helios. The clusters can be either on-premise or in the cloud. As a prerequisite to access FortKnox, you have to connect your clusters to Helios or ensure that the clusters are connected to Cohesity Helios. Also, the Access Permission toggle should be disabled when you are connecting a cluster to Helios. For more information, see Manage Cluster Connections in Cohesity Helios documentation.

Note: Cohesity FortKnox supports archiving data only from Cohesity Data Cloud (Self-managed) clusters running version 6.8 or later for AWS and version 7.x or later for Azure.

## Create Policies

Cohesity FortKnox uses the policies that are defined in a Cohesity cluster to archive data to a cloud vault. You can either choose any standard policies or create a custom policy before getting started with FortKnox. You can refer to the topic Create or Edit a Standard Policy in Cohesity documentation for more information.

Note: Cloud Vault can only be added to the policies from the Cohesity FortKnox and not from the Cohesity.

## Configure Host Mapping in Your Cluster

You can configure Cohesity FortKnox to use AWS DirectConnect and AWS PrivateLink for any communication between a Cohesity cluster and a cloud vault. As a prerequisite, you should configure a Host Mapping in your Cohesity cluster. For more information, see Manage Host Mappings in the Cohesity documentation.

Note: You can choose not to configure the host mapping in a Cohesity cluster and allow the data to be sent through internet.

## Firewall Ports

You should ensure that the following ports are open in your firewall for the Cohesity cluster.

[Get Started › Get Started]
Before you start on Cohesity FortKnox, it is important that you plan and decide on aspects such as:


- l Data from which cluster(s) should be vaulted in the cloud?
- l Which workloads such as Virtual Machines and Databases should be vaulted to the cloud?
- l In which Amazon Web Services region should the cloud vault be created?
- l How long do you want to retain the snapshots in a cloud vault?

- l Do you want to use Cohesity-managed key management service (KMS) or Selfmanaged KMS?

Note: Self-managed KMS option supports only Amazon Web Services KMS.

- l What would be the backup window ?


## Cohesity Clusters

Cohesity FortKnox vaults data from your cluster to the cloud. To achieve this, it's important for you to plan and decide on the clusters whose data will be sent to a cloud vault.
 After you decide on the clusters, you have to ensure that these clusters are associated with the Cohesity Helios account that includes Cohesity FortKnox. For more information on the supported cluster types, see Clusters.


## Workloads

Cohesity FortKnox allows you to recover workloads such as virtual machines and databases. For more information, see Supported Workloads, Clusters, and Regions.

For more information on workflows that are supported for each workload, see Supported Workflows.


## Snapshot Retention

The snapshots that are vaulted in the cloud vault are DataLocked by default and can be deleted after the retention period. Before you start using Cohesity FortKnox, It's important that you decide on how long you want to retain the snapshots in a cloud vault.

documents.title: Key Management
documents.text:
[Key Management › Key Management]
## Key Management

A Key Management Service (KMS) helps you manage the keys that encrypt data and secures it from unauthorized access. Cohesity FortKnox offers Cohesity managed KMS or you can bring your own AWS KMS keys if you are using an AWS vault.


## Cohesity KMS

You can use the Cohesity Managed Cloud KMS to encrypt your data in a cloud vault. It uses the Advanced Encryption Standard in Cipher Block Chaining mode using 256 bit Data Encryption Keys.


Note: You cannot change the key management service once the cloud vault is created.


Cohesity KMS generates and manages Data Encryption Keys (DEKs) and Key Encryption Keys (KEKs). When using AWS KMS, the cluster uses AWS APIs to generate DEKs and stores it securely. When using the Azure KMS, the cluster itself generates the DEKs.
 DEKs are stored in the cloud vault and are rotated periodically. Cohesity creates the cloud-based KMS key during tenant provisioning. The KEK material remains securely stored in the cloud and is never accessible to Cohesity.


## Amazon Web Services KMS

If you are using AWS vaults you can use your own AWS KMS keys to encrypt your data in a cloud vault. To use it, you have to get the AWS Encryption Key Amazon Resource Name (ARN). Cohesity FortKnox generates a Key Policy using your AWS Encryption Key ARN in JSON format.


Follow the steps to create a Key Policy JSON text. Before you start, refer to Create Cloud Vault and select your encryption option as Self-managed KMS (AWS Only) .

1. Enter your AWS Encryption Key ARN .
2. Select Get JSON .


![Image](/media/8d28293a-4280-41fd-a19a-b8a81f011a4c/06be006929d70085.png)

> **Figure:** Screenshot of the 'Create Cloud Vault' dialog showing fields for Vault Name, Select Region (AWS Asia Pacific (Sydney)), Storage Class (Warm Storage), and Select Encryption Option (Self Managed KMS).
 It includes a field to enter an AWS Encryption Key ARN and a 'Get JSON' button, with instructions to add generated JSON to the AWS KMS Key Policy. An error message indicates that the AWS Encryption Key ARN is required.

The Key Policy JSON format is generated.


You have to assign this Key Policy to an IAM role in your AWS environment. For more information on assigning a Key Policy to an IAM role, see Amazon Web Services Identity and Access Management User Guide .

[Prerequisites › Prerequisites]
1. Transfer to : Choose a cloud vault where you want to transfer or backup your data.
2. Every : Choose either Run or any time interval to determine how often data should be backed up to a Cloud Vault. This defines the protection schedule for capturing backups.
3. Retain for : Specify for how many days the backups are retained in a Cloud Vault.
4. l For AWS, the minimum retention allowed is 30 days for warm vault and 90 days for cold vault.

- l For Azure, the minimum retention allowed is 30 days for warm vault and 120 days for cold vault.

You can configure different retention time for different policies. For Free Trial users, the retention period is set to 30 days.

Note: By default, DataLock is enabled for backups to Cloud Vault. This means the data cannot be deleted once it is sent to the vault till it expires. After the expiry date, the data will be automatically removed.

4. You can optionally choose to Transfer only successful runs .
5. Select Add .
6. On the Cloud Vault Protection page, select Continue .

The Cloud Vault Quorum Group page appears.

You've added Cloud Vault Protection to the policy in your cluster. The vaulting task to the cloud vault is initiated in the next protection run.

Note: You can view the vault added to the policy from the Cohesity Data Cloud (Self-managed), however, you cannot modify it. Vaulting can be configured only from the Policies tab in the Protection page in Cohesity FortKnox.

## Create Cloud Vault Quorum Group

In Cohesity FortKnox, you can define a group of users called a quorum group who can collectively decide whether the operations initiated by a FortKnox user are allowed to be executed or not.

Follow the steps below to create a quorum group.

1. Select Create Quorum Group .
2. Under Group Details , enter the Name of the quorum group, choose an Operation Target , and add a Description (Optional).
3. Under Operations , Recover from FortKnox Vault and Recover Metadata from FortKnox Vault are selected by default.

Note: An operation can be assigned to only one quorum group. This means an operation, for example, Recover from FortKnox Vault , can be approved by only one Quorum group.

4. Under Approvers , add the members of the quorum group. The list of members are populated based on the users available in your Cohesity Data Cloud account.
5. Set the Approval Quorum . You can either select All Members or set a minimum value of members required to approve any requests.
6. Set Approval Workflow . You can enter a time value after which the defined action, either Accept or Deny , will be taken automatically.
7. Select Create . You've created the quorum group.
8. Select Complete .

The Dashboard page appears.

You've now successfully completed the onboarding steps to access Cohesity FortKnox .

[Edit Policies › Edit Policies]
## Edit Policies

In Cohesity FortKnox, you can edit the policies that are available in the Cohesity clusters associated with the Cohesity Data Cloud user account and add Cloud Vault configurations to policies.

A policy is a reusable set of settings that define how and when objects are protected, replicated and vaulted. You select which standard policy to use when configuring a Protection Group. A Protection Group uses the schedules and settings defined in the policy to determine when and how backups are captured, vaulted or replicated.

You can use the default standard policies or create your own custom policies.

Tip: Policies eliminate the effort to repetitively define the same settings for different sources and protection groups and therefore, saves time for you.

Note: When a policy includes a Cloud Vault, Smart Retention Adjustment protects your local backups from being deleted before your data is safely copied to its secondary target. If a Cloud Vault (or Replication or Archive) task is cancelled or fails after a successful local backup, Smart Retention Adjustment extends the retention of the local copy to match the failed target's retention. Smart Retention Adjustment is enabled by default. For more information, see Smart Retention Adjustment.

question: I just created a new backup repository in Veeam Backup & Replication for my Veeam Agent for Oracle Solaris machines. Can the Solaris agents write to it straight away, and does it matter that the repository uses KMS encryption?
gold_facts: A newly created backup repository has access permissions set to Deny to everyone, so users must be granted access before they can store backups there.
The default backup repository is set to Allow to everyone right after installation (for testing/evaluation).
Veeam Agent for Oracle Solaris does not support Veeam backup repositories with KMS encryption enabled.
Access permissions are not needed when backups go through Veeam Agent backup jobs managed by Veeam Backup & Replication (it uses a TLS certificate instead).

B.text:
**Veeam Backup & Replication:** Veeam Backup & Replication does not allow using KMS keys for data encryption with a Veeam Agent backup policy [4], and it communicates with the KMS server to retrieve encryption keys when KMS keys are chosen for backup file encryption [8]. Repositories with enabled KMS encryption are not supported as a backup repository for Veeam Agent [3].

**Veeam Agent for Oracle Solaris:** The Solaris agent can store backup files on backup repositories managed by Veeam Backup & Replication [13], and it uses the Default Backup Repository as a backup destination [9]. However, Veeam Agent for Oracle Solaris does not support Veeam backup repositories with enabled KMS encryption [1]. Encryption for jobs targeting a Veeam Backup & Replication repository is managed by a backup administrator in Veeam Backup & Replication, and the agent cannot use the --setencryption or --resetencryption options against such a repository [6].

So the agents can write to a Veeam Backup & Replication–managed repository, but a repository with KMS encryption enabled is not supported for Veeam Agent for Oracle Solaris [1].

documents.title: Managing Backup Repositories
documents.text:
[Managing Backup Repositories › Managing Backup Repositories]
Managing Backup Repositories
============================

A backup repository is a storage location where Veeam Agent keeps backup files. You can use the following types of disk\-based storage as a target location for a backup job:


* Local (internal) storage of the protected machine (not recommended)
* Direct attached storage (DAS), such as USB, eSATA or Firewire external drives
* Network Attached Storage (NAS) able to represent itself as SMB (CIFS) or NFS share
* Veeam Backup \& Replication 13\.1 backup repository


| Important |
| --- |

| Consider the following about backup repositories:* \[For local storage] A backup repository should be created on a separate volume from a volume that contains data you plan to back up. * \[For Veeam backup repository] Veeam Cloud Connect repositories, repositories with enabled KMS encryption and object storage repositories managed by Veeam Backup \& Replication are not supported. |


In This Section

* [Creating Backup Repository](backup_repo_create.html)
* [Viewing List of Backup Repositories](backup_repo_list.html)
* [Editing Backup Repository](backup_repo_edit.html)

documents.title: Backup Repository
documents.text:
[Backup Repository › Backup Repository]
Backup Repository
=================

A backup job configured in Veeam Agent creates backup files in a backup repository. A backup repository is a directory on the storage where you want to keep backup files. You can use the following types of disk\-based storage as a backup repository:


* Local (internal) storage of the protected machine (not recommended)
* Direct attached storage (DAS), such as USB, eSATA or Firewire external drives
* Network Attached Storage (NAS) able to represent itself as SMB (CIFS) or NFS share
* Veeam Backup \& Replication 13\.1 backup repository


| Important |
| --- |

| Consider the following about backup repositories:* \[For local storage] A backup repository should be created on a separate volume from a volume that contains data you plan to back up. * \[For Veeam backup repository] Veeam Cloud Connect repositories, repositories with enabled KMS encryption and object storage repositories managed by Veeam Backup \& Replication are not supported. |


The way you work with backup repositories depends on where you want to store backup files.


* If you want to keep backup files on a local storage, remote storage or in a network shared folder, you must create a backup repository. You must perform this task in advance, before you configure the backup job.
 When you create a backup repository, you specify a local directory in which Veeam Agent will create backup files and a name for the backup repository. To learn more, see [Creating Backup Repository](backup_repo_create.html).


If you back up your data to a remote storage or network shared folder, you must mount this remote location to the specified local directory before you start a backup job. Veeam Agent does not check whether the remote backup location is mounted to the local directory. If the remote location is not mounted, Veeam Agent will create a new backup chain directly in the local directory. Besides, if the directory to which the remote location should be mounted resides on the backed\-up volume, a backup job may fail.


* If you want to keep backup files on a Veeam backup repository, you do not need to create repositories. Before configuring the backup job, you must connect to the Veeam backup server. Veeam Agent will obtain information about backup repositories managed by this backup server. To learn more, see [Connecting to Veeam Backup Server](manage_vbr_add.html).


You can configure several backup repositories and target different backup jobs at these repositories. This may be useful if you want to back up different types of data to separate locations or to keep several copies of your backed\-up data.

Related Tasks

[Managing Backup Repositories](backup_repo.html)

System Requirements
===================

The protected Mac computer must meet requirements listed in the table below.

**System Requirements**

| Specification | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| Hardware | The protected Mac computer must meet the following hardware requirements:* CPU: x64 or ARM Apple\-branded hardware. * Memory: 2 GB RAM or more. Memory consumption varies depending on the total amount of backed\-up data. * Disk Space: 600 MB free disk space for product installation. * Network: 10 Mbps or faster network connection to a backup target. |

| OS | Veeam Agent supports the following macOS versions:* 26 Tahoe * 15 Sequoia * 14 Sonoma * 13 Ventura * 12 Monterey * 11 Big Sur |

| File System | Veeam Agent supports consistent data backup with snapshot for the APFS file system. The following file systems can be backed up in the [snapshot\-less mode](backup_hiw.html#snapshotless):* HFS\+ * MS\-DOS (FAT) * exFAT * NTFS * FAT32 * SMB  
Consider the following:* Software RAID is not supported. * Backup of files from a cloud storage mounted under the /Users/\<user\_name\>/Library/CloudStorage/ directory is not supported. * Total size of all file systems included in a file\-level backup must not exceed 216 TiB. * Size of a file in a backup must not exceed 16 TiB. * Name of a file in a backup must not be larger than 254 bytes.  Keep in mind that characters that you can use in the file name may be encoded in 2 bytes or more.*
 Sparse files are not supported. Veeam Agent backs up and restores sparse files as regular files. * Veeam Agent automatically excludes from backup the files that have the following extended attribute: com.apple.metadata:com\_apple\_backup\_excludeItem. |


Backup Target

Backup can be performed to the following types of storage:

* On\-premises or cloud\-based object storage
* Local (internal) storage of the protected computer (not recommended)
* Direct attached storage (DAS), such as USB, eSATA or Firewire external drives
* Network Attached Storage (NAS) able to represent itself as SMB (CIFS) share

* Veeam Backup \& Replication version 13\.1 backup repository (including deduplication appliances)

* Veeam Cloud Connect 13\.1 cloud repository


| Important |
| --- |
| Consider the following about backup repositories:* \[For local storage] A backup repository should be created on a separate volume from a volume that contains data you plan to back up. * \[For Veeam backup repository] Backup repositories with enabled KMS encryption are not supported. |

documents.title: Storage Settings
documents.text:
[Storage Settings › Storage Settings]

* If you change a password for data encryption for an existing backup policy targeted at a Veeam backup repository without changing other backup policy settings, the process of applying the backup policy to a protected computer completes with a notification informing that the backup policy was not modified. This happens because data encryption settings for managed Veeam Agents are saved to the Veeam Backup \& Replication database and are not passed to a Veeam Agent computer.
* If you enable or disable encryption for an existing Veeam Agent backup policy, during the next session Veeam Agent will create a full backup file.
* Encryption is not retroactive. If you enable encryption for an existing backup policy, Veeam Agent will encrypt the backup chain starting from the next restore point created with this policy.
* When you enable data encryption for a backup policy, Veeam Backup \& Replication uses the specified password to encrypt backups of all Veeam Agent computers added to the backup policy. A Veeam Agent computer user can restore data from the backup of this computer without providing a password to decrypt backup. To restore data from a backup of another computer in this backup policy, a user must provide a password specified in the backup policy settings.

This scenario differs from the same scenario in earlier versions of Veeam Backup \& Replication where all backups created for Veeam Agent computers in the backup policy could be accessed from any computer in the backup policy without providing a password.

To learn more about data encryption in Veeam Backup \& Replication, see [Data Encryption](data_encryption.html).

Viewing Backups
===============

To view a list of backups created by a backup job configured in Veeam Agent for Oracle Solaris, use the following command:


| veeamconfig backup list \[\-\-all] |
| --- |

Where \-\-all is an option that instructs Veeam Agent to display information about all Veeam Agent for Oracle Solaris backups in backup repositories configured in the product. If you do not use this option, Veeam Agent will display information about backups of the current Veeam Agent machine only.


If you work with Veeam Agent connected to a Veeam backup server as a member of a protection group for pre\-installed Veeam Agents, for security reasons, the veeamconfig backup list \-\-all command will display backups created only by the current Veeam Agent computer with the current connection settings.
 To learn more about protection groups for pre\-installed Veeam Agents, see the [Protection Group Types](https://helpcenter.veeam.com/docs/vbr/userguide/agents_protection_groups_types.html?ver=13) section in the Veeam Backup \& Replication User Guide.


For each backup, Veeam Agent displays the following information:

**Viewing Backups**

Step 10\. Review Backup Job Settings
====================================

You can store backup files created with Veeam Agent on backup repositories managed by Veeam Backup \& Replication. To do this, you must select a Veeam Backup \& Replication backup repository as a target location in the properties of the backup job.
 To learn more about supported backup repositories, see the [Backup Repositories](https://helpcenter.veeam.com/docs/backup/vsphere/backup_repository.html?ver=120) and [Scale\-Out Backup Repositories](https://helpcenter.veeam.com/docs/backup/vsphere/backup_repository_sobr.html?ver=120) sections in the Veeam Backup \& Replication User Guide.

| Consider the following:* The current guide covers subjects related to Veeam Agent operating in the standalone mode.

A.text:
No — after you create a new backup repository, access permissions are set to Deny to everyone, so you must grant users access permissions before they can store backups there [1][3]. You grant permissions in the Backup Infrastructure view by selecting the repository and clicking Set Access Permissions (or right-click → Access permissions), then choosing who to allow in the Standalone applications tab [1].

Also, KMS encryption matters: Veeam Agent for Oracle Solaris does not support Veeam backup repositories with enabled KMS encryption [1][6], so you cannot use that repository as a backup target.

documents.title: Setting Up User Permissions on Backup Repositories
documents.text:
Setting Up User Permissions on Backup Repositories

To be able to store backups in a backup repository managed by a Veeam backup server, the user must have access permissions on this backup repository. 

| IMPORTANT |
| --- |
| Veeam Agent for Oracle Solaris does not support Veeam backup repositories with enabled KMS encryption. To learn more about KMS encryption for Veeam backup repositories, see the [Key Management System Keys](https://helpcenter.veeam.com/docs/vbr/userguide/kms.html?ver=13) section in the Veeam Backup \& Replication User Guide. |

| NOTE |
| --- |
| If you plan to create backups in a Veeam backup repository with Veeam Agent backup jobs configured in Veeam Backup \& Replication, you do not need to grant access permissions on the backup repository to users. In the Veeam Agent management scenario, to establish a connection between the backup server and protected computers, Veeam Backup \& Replication uses a TLS certificate. To learn more, see the [Configuring Security Settings](https://helpcenter.veeam.com/docs/vbr/userguide/agents_manage_tls_and_ssh.html?ver=13) section in the Veeam Backup \& Replication User Guide. |

Access permissions are granted to security principals such as users and AD groups by the backup administrator working with Veeam Backup \& Replication. Users with granted access permissions can target Veeam Agent backup jobs at this backup repository and perform restore from backups located in this backup repository.

Right after installation, access permissions on the default backup repository are set to Allow to everyone for testing and evaluation purposes. If necessary, you can change these settings.

After you create a new backup repository, access permissions on this repository are set to Deny to everyone. To allow users to store backups in the backup repository, you must grant users with access permissions to this repository.

To grant access permissions to a security principal:

1. In Veeam Backup \& Replication, open the Backup Infrastructure view.
2. In the inventory pane, click one of the following nodes:

* The Backup Repositories node — if you want to grant access permissions on a regular backup repository to Veeam Agent users.
* The Scale\-out Repositories node — if you want to grant access permissions on a scale\-out backup repository to Veeam Agent users.

1. In the working area, select the necessary backup repository and click Set Access Permissions on the ribbon, or right\-click the backup repository and select Access permissions. If you do not see the Set Access Permissions button on the ribbon or the Access permissions command is not available in the shortcut menu, press and hold the \[Ctrl] key, right\-click the backup repository and select Access permissions.

[

![Set Up User Permissions on Backup Repositories](/media/115e0d8c-babf-49f6-a562-93e6ddbb8f88/e265fc866340.png)

> **Figure:** Screenshot of the Veeam Backup and Replication interface showing the Backup Repository section. The context menu for the 'Object Storage (S3)' repository is open, with the 'Access permissions...' option highlighted, indicating the action to set user permissions for the selected backup repository.

](images/ep_permissions.png "Set Up User Permissions on Backup Repositories")

> **Figure:** Screenshot of the Veeam Backup and Replication interface showing the Backup Repository section. The context menu for the 'Object Storage (S3)' repository is open, with the 'Access permissions...' option highlighted, indicating the action to set user permissions for the selected backup repository.

1. In the Access Permissions window, in the Standalone applications tab, specify to whom you want to grant access permissions on this backup repository:

* Allow to everyone — select this option if you want all users to be able to store backups on this backup repository. Setting access permissions to Everyone is equal to granting access rights to the Everyone Microsoft Windows group (Anonymous users are excluded). However, we recommend this scenario for demo environments only.
* Allow to the following accounts or groups only — select this option if you want only specific users to be able to store backups on this backup repository. Click Add to add the necessary users and groups to the list.

| TIP |
| --- |
| If you want to back up data to Veeam Backup \& Replication on Linux with a local Veeam appliance user, specify a user with the Service Account role. This role allows access to the Veeam backup repository and does not require the password rotation. To learn more about available local user roles, see the [Managing Users and Roles](https://helpcenter.veeam.com/docs/vbr/userguide/hmc_users.html?ver=13) section in the Veeam Backup \& Replication User Guide. |

Integration with Veeam Backup & Replication
Integration with Veeam Backup \& Replication

| Important |
| --- |
| Veeam Agent for Oracle Solaris version 13\.1 requires Veeam Backup \& Replication version 13\.1. |

You can store backup files created with Veeam Agent on backup repositories managed by Veeam Backup \& Replication. To do this, you must select a Veeam Backup \& Replication backup repository as a target location in the properties of the backup job. To learn more about supported backup repositories, see the [Backup Repositories](https://helpcenter.veeam.com/docs/backup/vsphere/backup_repository.html?ver=120) and [Scale\-Out Backup Repositories](https://helpcenter.veeam.com/docs/backup/vsphere/backup_repository_sobr.html?ver=120) sections in the Veeam Backup \& Replication User Guide.

| NOTE |
| --- |
| Consider the following:* The current guide covers subjects related to Veeam Agent operating in the standalone mode. * You can also use Veeam Backup \& Replication to manage Veeam Agent on computers in your infrastructure. As part of the Veeam Agent management scenario, you can remotely deploy Veeam Agent to your computers, as well as configure and manage Veeam Agent backup jobs in Veeam Backup \& Replication. To learn more, see the [Veeam Agent Backup](https://helpcenter.veeam.com/docs/vbr/userguide/protect_comp.html?ver=13) section in the Veeam Backup \& Replication User Guide. * If you create a backup job with the Veeam Agent command line interface, you need to specify a Veeam backup repository in the backup job settings. Veeam backup repository appears in the list of backup repositories after you connect to a Veeam backup server. To learn more, see [Managing Veeam Backup \& Replication Servers](manage_vbr.html). |

Veeam Agent works with the Veeam Backup \& Replication backup repository as with any other backup repository. Backup files are stored to a separate folder; you can perform standard restore operations using these files.

Information about Veeam Agent backups stored on the Veeam Backup \& Replication backup repositories, backup jobs and sessions becomes available in the Veeam Backup \& Replication console:

* The Veeam Agent backup job is displayed in the list of jobs in Veeam Backup \& Replication.
* Backup files created with Veeam Agent are displayed in the list of backups, under the Agents node.
* Performed job sessions are available in the History view of Veeam Backup \& Replication.

Backup administrators working with Veeam Backup \& Replication can perform a set of operations with Veeam Agent backups:

* Perform [data protection operations](performing_data_protection_tas.html).
* Perform [restore operations](performing_restore_tasks.html).
* Perform [administrative tasks](integration_administration.html).

Related Task

[Using with Veeam Backup \& Replication](integrate.html)

documents.title: System Requirements
documents.text:
System Requirements

A machine that you plan to protect with Veeam Agent for Oracle Solaris must meet requirements listed in the table below.

**System Requirements**

| Specification | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| Hardware | CPU: Oracle SPARC or Intel x86 processor. Memory: Memory: 1 GB RAM (for standard backup and restore operations) / 4 GB RAM (for bare metal recovery). Disk space: 250 MB free disk space for product installation. Network: 10 Mbps or faster network connection to a backup target. |
| OS | Oracle Solaris 10 1/13, 11\.3 and 11\.4 on machines based on the SPARC and Intel x86 architecture. Note: Only GA versions and updates of the Oracle Solaris OS that have been released before version 13\.1 of Veeam Agent for Oracle Solaris are supported. |
| File System | All file systems supported by the supported operating systems. Note: * Total size of all file systems included in a file\-level backup must not exceed 218 TB. * Size of a file in a backup must not exceed 16 TiB. * Name of a file in a backup must not be larger than 254 bytes.  Keep in mind that characters that you can use in the file name may be encoded in 2 bytes or more.* Sparse files are not supported. Veeam Agent backs up and restores sparse files as regular files. * Backup of clustered systems is not supported. |
| Software | The system must have the following utilities installed:* mlocate (version 0\.26\-1 or later) – required for file system indexing. If your system does not have the mlocate utility, you can install it from the product installation media. * tar \- required for file system indexing, exporting and rotating logs. It is installed with the product. * gzip – required for file system indexing, exporting and rotating logs. It must be installed separately. * xorriso – required for creating Veeam Recovery Media.  Oracle Solaris minimal install (Core System Support Software Group) requires adding the following packages: SUNWtoo, SUNWzoneu and SUNWzoner. |

Backup Target

Backup can be performed to the following types of storage:

* On\-premises or cloud\-based object storage.

* Local (internal) storage of the protected machine (not recommended).
* Direct attached storage (DAS), such as USB, eSATA or Firewire external drives.
* Network Attached Storage (NAS) able to represent itself as NFS or SMB (CIFS) share.

* Veeam Backup \& Replication 13\.1 backup repository.

| Important |
| --- |
| Consider the following about backup repositories:* \[For local storage] A backup repository should be created on a separate volume from a volume that contains data you plan to back up. * \[For Veeam backup repositories] Veeam Cloud Connect repositories and repositories with KMS encryption enabled are not supported. |

Network

Consider the following:

* Veeam Agent does not support Kerberos authentication.

* If you back up to a repository managed by a Veeam backup server, Veeam Agent must be able to establish a direct IP connection to the Veeam Backup \& Replication server. Veeam Agent cannot work with Veeam Backup \& Replication that is located behind a NAT gateway.
* Domain names of the Veeam Agent machine, Veeam Backup \& Replication server and other servers in the Veeam backup infrastructure must be resolvable into IPv4 or IPv6 addresses.

question: With Veeam Agent for IBM AIX, what happens to the backup chain if I turn on encryption for an existing job, change its password later, or turn encryption off?
gold_facts: Enabling encryption makes the next job session create a full backup, and it and later incrementals are encrypted.
Changing the password of an already encrypted job makes the next session create a new incremental backup encrypted with the new password.
Disabling encryption makes the next job session create a full backup.

[Data Encryption Settings › Data Encryption Settings]
Data Encryption Settings
========================

If you want to encrypt the content of backup files, at the Advanced step of the wizard, specify data encryption settings for the backup job.


| Note |
| --- |
| The Backup encryption option is unavailable if you have chosen to save backup files on a Veeam backup repository. Encryption options for Veeam Agent backup jobs targeted at the backup repository are managed by a backup administrator working with Veeam Backup \& Replication.

To enable backup encryption, do the following:


1. In the Specify advanced job settings window, select the Backup encryption option with the \[Tab] key and press \[Enter].
2. In the Encryption window, make sure that the Enable backup file encryption option is selected and press \[Space].
3. In the Password field, type a password that you want to use for encryption.
4. In the Hint field, type a hint for the password. In case you lose the password, the specified hint will help you to remember the lost password.
5. Switch to the Ok button and press \[Enter].

documents.title: Data Encryption
documents.text:
[Data Encryption › Data Encryption]
Data Encryption
===============

Data security is an important part of the backup strategy. You must protect your information from unauthorized access, especially if you back up sensitive data to remote locations. To keep your data safe, you can use data encryption.


Data encryption transforms data to an unreadable, scrambled format with the help of a cryptographic algorithm and a secret key. If encrypted data is intercepted, it cannot be unlocked and read by the eavesdropper. Only intended recipients who know the secret key can reverse encrypted information back to a readable format.


Encryption is performed on the trusted side depending on the backup target:

* Encryption is performed on the source side for all backup targets except the Veeam backup repository.
* Encryption is performed on the target side if you store backups in the Veeam backup repository.


Decryption is performed on the same side as encryption.


To create encrypted backups, you must enable the encryption option and specify a password that will be used for data encryption. To learn more, see [Data Encryption Settings](backup_job_encryption.html).


| NOTE |
| --- |
| You cannot specify encryption options for the backup job if you have chosen to save Veeam Agent backups in a Veeam backup repository. For such jobs, encryption options are managed per repository by a backup administrator working with Veeam Backup \& Replication.
 To learn more, see the [Encrypting Standalone Application Backups in Backup Repositories](https://helpcenter.veeam.com/docs/vbr/userguide/encrypting_backups.html?ver=13) section in the Veeam Backup \& Replication User Guide. |


In This Section

* [How Data Encryption Works](encryption_hiw.html)
* [How Data Decryption Works](decryption_hiw.html)


Related Tasks

* [Creating Backup Jobs](backup_job_create.html)
* [Restoring Data from Encrypted Backups](restore_encrypted.html)

[Importing Backups › Importing Backups]

Importing Encrypted Backups

You can import an encrypted backup created by Veeam Agent for IBM AIX into the Veeam Agent database. This operation is required if you want to restore data from an encrypted backup created by Veeam Agent for IBM AIX running on another machine. Note that you cannot import backups that reside in a Veeam Backup \& Replication repository.

To import an encrypted backup:

1. Start the import process with the following command:

| veeamconfig backup import \-\-path \<path\> |
| --- |

where \<path\> is a path to the VBM file of the backup that you want to import.

For example:

| user@srv01:\~$ veeamconfig backup import \-\-path /home/share/srv15\\ Backup/Backup.vbm |
| --- |

* During standard file\-level restore if you want to restore data from an encrypted backup file created by Veeam Agent on another machine.
